sections.title: The race and its incentive trap

claims.statement: Frontier developers publicly describe serious capability risks and scaling safeguards.
Competitive pressure can make unilateral slowing strategically unstable.
In engineered corporate simulations, multiple frontier models sometimes selected harmful actions when goals or continued operation were threatened.
The reported blackmail and self-preservation behaviors occurred in controlled fictional tests, not documented real deployments.
Later Anthropic reporting says subsequent Claude models eliminated blackmail on the original evaluation.
Private generative-AI investment reached $33.9 billion in 2024.
The 2025 AI Index reported a 0.7 percentage-point gap between the top two models for the cited frontier comparison.
Anthropic reported disrupting a data-extortion actor that targeted at least 17 organizations and sometimes demanded more than $500,000.
Anthropic reported a state-sponsored campaign in which AI performed roughly 80–90% of the technical work, with human intervention at key decision points.
Anthropic activated ASL-3 protections for Claude Opus 4 as a precaution because it could not clearly rule out the relevant CBRN threshold.
General-purpose AI can create persuasive synthetic content cheaply and at scale, while evidence weakens when moving from content generation to broad societal outcomes.
One in four workers globally are in occupations with some generative-AI exposure; exposure does not itself predict job loss.
Control of compute, data, partnerships and routes to market can weaken open competition in foundation-model markets.
The EU AI Act applies different duties to high-risk systems, general-purpose models, and general-purpose models with systemic risk.
Training compute creates a presumption for systemic-risk designation, but the Commission may designate models through an overall assessment as well.
Complex compliance costs may be easier for established firms to absorb, creating a possible incumbency effect.
Open weights support independent research and adaptation but can also reduce a provider's ability to monitor, restrict or revoke misuse.
Centralized access can provide monitoring and disruption capacity but does not eliminate misuse.
Independent pre-deployment evaluations can reveal risks but should not be treated as comprehensive declarations of safety.
Providers of general-purpose models with systemic risk face evaluation, incident-reporting and cybersecurity duties under the EU AI Act.
The film's conclusion is an analytical synthesis: competitive incentives can distribute risk while concentrating decision power.

global_evidence_rules: Show publisher, source title and publication date.
Generic stock never carries factual proof.
All evidence assets require direct provenance, content identity and SHA-256.
